linkedin.title: I started building a news app when I was a teenager because I was tired of missing the stories that actually mattered.
linkedin.body:
It felt like I was drowning in noise. Every time I opened a news site, I had to dig through endless headlines just to find the one or two updates that impacted my day. The technology was there to filter this, but the experience was always cluttered and impersonal.

That frustration led to the first version of what would become Headlinne. I realized that the problem wasn't a lack of information. It was the lack of relevance. We are constantly told to consume more content, but we rarely have the tools to consume better content.

Building this as a young founder taught me a hard lesson. Algorithms shouldn't just keep you scrolling. They should respect your time. True personalization isn't about guessing what you want to click on. It is about understanding what you need to know to stay informed without the mental fatigue.

We are now taking that same philosophy to build something that cuts through the noise. It is not about reinventing the news. It is about making the news work for you again.
linkedin.cta: You can see how we are doing things differently at HEADLINNE.com.

reels.title: Falling inflation does not mean falling prices

beats.caption: Why prices never actually drop
beats.detail: Even when the inflation rate slows down, your grocery bill stays high.
beats.narration: You hear that inflation is cooling off, but your grocery bill is still sky

beats.caption: Inflation vs Prices
beats.detail: They are not the same thing.
beats.narration: That is because inflation is just the speed at which prices are climbing.

beats.caption: The Coffee Example
beats.narration: Think of a cup of coffee that cost five dollars last year and six dollars

beats.caption: Growth is slowing
beats.narration: If inflation slows, that coffee might cost six dollars and ten cents next

beats.caption: Higher, just slower
beats.detail: Cooling inflation is not a discount.
beats.narration: The price is still higher than before, it is just rising at a slower pace.

beats.caption: Lower inflation just means slower rises
beats.narration: Lower inflation just means prices are rising more slowly, not coming back

reels.caption:
Why does everything still feel so expensive even when inflation is supposedly falling?

Inflation measures the rate of change, not the price tag itself. When inflation cools, it means prices are rising less quickly, not that they are decreasing. It is the difference between a car slowing down and a car shifting into reverse.
